prompt: Given coin values and an amount, return the fewest coins that add up to the amount, or −1 if impossible.
tells: fewest coins that add up to the amount
why: Unbounded knapsack: best[a] = 1 + min best[a − coin] over every coin.
trap: Greedy (largest coin first) fails for coins like 1, 3, 4 and amount 6.

prompt: Can an array of positive integers be split into two subsets with equal sums?
why: Subset sum to total/2: a boolean table over reachable sums, one item at a time.
trap: Subsets aren't contiguous, so prefix sums don't help.

prompt: How many different combinations of coins make up a given amount, if each coin can be used any number of times?
why: Loop coins outside, amounts inside: ways[a] += ways[a − coin]. That counts each combination once.
trap: Looping amounts outside counts orderings (1+2 and 2+1) separately.

prompt: Put a + or − in front of each number so the total equals a target. In how many ways can you do it?
tells: + or − in front of each number
why: Picking the + set P means sum(P) = (total + target) / 2: count subsets with that sum.
trap: Trying every sign is 2ⁿ; the subset-sum rewrite makes it a capacity table.

prompt: Each gadget has a price and a value. With a budget of 1,000, choose gadgets (each at most once) to maximize total value.
why: 0/1 knapsack: best[b] = max(best[b], best[b − price] + value), iterating budget downward.
trap: Taking the best value-per-dollar first fails when a big item doesn't fit evenly.
